name: Tute cabrero
description: Tute cabrero is a point-trick elimination game for 3 to 6 players, popular in Argentina and Uruguay. Each deal you aim either to take no tricks or to finish with the highest or lowest point total; middle totals lose. Four losses eliminate a player; the last one or two remaining win. Uses the standard 40-card Spanish deck with follow-suit and optional singing (declaring king-horse for 20 or 40 points after winning a trick).

content.text: Tute cabrero is a point-trick elimination game for 3 to 6 players, popular in Argentina and Uruguay. Each deal you aim either to take no tricks or to finish with the highest or lowest point total; middle totals lose. Four losses eliminate a player; the last one or two remaining win. Uses the standard 40-card Spanish deck with follow-suit and optional singing (declaring king-horse for 20 or 40 points after winning a trick).

Tute originated in Italy as tutti and spread to Spain in the 19th century, becoming one of the most popular card games there. Tute cabrero is an individual-play variant for 3 to 6 players, popular in Argentina and Uruguay. It uses the same 40-card Spanish deck and marriage-style point-trick structure as partnership Tute but with elimination (four losses) and a first-hand rule that coins are trumps and the holder of the two of coins leads. The variant is described in Spanish card-game literature and on dedicated Tute Cabrero pages.
Three to six players, each playing for themselves.
Counter-clockwise; 8 each (5–6p), 10 each (4p), or 13 each plus one to centre (3p). First hand coins are trumps; later hands last card to mano turned for trump.
